payload.text: **TRAPS FROM THE SQLITE BUMP AND DETECTOR SESSION (cc, the fifth localfold of 2026-09-17; watch-outs 47 to 50 hold the earlier ones).** **A WITNESS THAT CANNOT SEE THE EVENT IS NOT A WITNESS, AND INDEPENDENCE IS WORTHLESS WITHOUT VISIBILITY.** I recommended a shadow-table anti-join as the independent half of the 0442 detector, on the ground that it never reads an index segment and so cannot be misled by segment damage; vc ruled it in; I then measured it against the actual damaged store and it reads **0 against non-empty populations of 829 and 829**, while the index-side query finds the fault in 0.13 s. **The property I was selecting for and the property that disqualifies it are the same property.** Worse, a decoy second witness is more dangerous than one acknowledged witness, because it manufactures confidence -- which is the exact shape of `doctor` and `index status` reading clean over real damage. **Declaring a principle unsatisfied beats satisfying it with a decoy**, and where two available witnesses share a failure mode, say so in the output rather than omitting it. I argued myself into this immediately after catching its neighbour, the trap that `fts5vocab` is itself an index reader and so not independent of the checker. **QUOTE A SPECIFICATION, NEVER PARAPHRASE IT INTO A DESIGN.** hv decision 25 says "a document present IN THE INDEX with no row in the content table". I substituted "present in a shadow table" and called it a refinement; vc read the same sentence, ruled on my restatement, and did not go back to the source text. Two nodes drifted off one sentence in the same direction. **A DIFF IS NOT EVIDENCE UNTIL ITS INPUTS ARE SHOWN NON-EMPTY.** I printed "TOKENIZER ARG PARSER: IDENTICAL" from diffing two files that were both zero lines -- the awk matched nothing, and empty-versus-empty reads as agreement at exit 0, in the output shape that looks most like proof. A `wc -l` I had added for an unrelated reason is the only thing that caught it. A negative from an empty population is not a weak finding, it is the absence of a finding wearing one, so a comparison instrument needs its population asserted exactly as a census does. **FOUR OF MY INSTRUMENTS LIED IN ONE SESSION AND THREE REPORTED SUCCESS WHILE DOING NOTHING.** `find -newermt` is REFUSED by bfs and prints nothing at exit 0, so a "zero files changed" reading was a false zero (this was already in a shared memory and I met it anyway). A scanner reported a multi-statement SQL offender that was a `;` inside a PROSE COMMENT. A `perl -pi` anchored `^///` against doc lines indented two spaces inside `impl`, edited nothing, reported success, and `set -e` did not fire -- **an edit that matches nothing is indistinguishable from one that worked unless you check the RESULT rather than the exit code.** And the empty diff above. **REGION-BOUND ANY GREP OF THE SQLITE AMALGAMATION.** fts3/fts4 and the core SQL parser live in the same file as fts5, and several of their messages read like fts5's: I sent dc ten expression-fault strings of which **three were not fts5's**, and the dangerous one is an unprefixed `syntax error near "` which is the CORE PARSER's -- allowlisting it would classify a malformed SQL statement as an FTS5 expression fault on the `search_sql` door, which is issue 0443's own defect arriving through 0443's fix. The bounds are the amalgamation's own `Begin file fts5.c` marker: 231419-257320 at 3.46.0, 241057-269022 at 3.53.2. dc caught it by **refusing to transcribe my prose and demanding the artefact**, which is the practice, not the exception: **put the strings in a banked file and hand over the ref, never re-type them into a message.** `unterminated string` has two byte-identical homes, core at 83134 and fts5 at 236905, so an equality test on it is not evidence of which engine raised it. A `%s` immediately after a prefix defeats a `starts_with` match -- `"fts5: %s queries are not supported (detail!=full)"` substitutes a closed set of exactly two, `"phrase"` or `"NEAR"`, read from the call site. **A PREFIX COUNT IS A DISCRIMINATOR THAT CAN ROT UNDER A DEP BUMP**: `fts5: ` prefixed messages go from 8 to 14 between 3.46.0 and 3.53.2 and all six additions mean CORRUPTION, so a prefix-only recogniser would tell a reader their query is malformed because the store is corrupt. **A SAFE DEFAULT IS ASYMMETRIC PROTECTION** (vc's form): it covers the fall-through and not the FALSE MATCH, so "we default to the store fault" is never a reason to loosen a discriminator. **ON THIS FILESYSTEM `F-x` AND `f-x` ARE ONE FILE WHILE ZSH'S GLOB IS CASE-SENSITIVE**, so a script can write a file it then cannot glob, and silently overwrite a differently-cased file it meant to keep -- which is how an earlier extraction clobbered its own inputs. **`git patch-id` NEEDS GIT-FORMAT HEADERS**: a plain `diff -u` yields no patch-id at all, silently, so a bank meant to be judged by patch-id needs `diff --git a/... b/...` lines prepended. And **a version-specific citation in a doc comment is a maintenance edge a dep bump finds**: `store.rs:3199` cites rusqlite by version AND file:line, and the bump moves both -- the citation was wrong while every other sentence in that comment stayed true, and the comment's own thesis (a dependency default is invisible to source review) was strengthened by the default surviving eight minors and shifting one line without telling anyone.
